text: Ask HN: How do you manage your AI agents' context across clients and projects? | Hacker News Hacker News new | past | comments | ask | show | jobs | submit login Ask HN: How do you manage your AI agents' context across clients and projects? 8 points by Michel_Aventin 1 hour ago | hide | past | favorite | 2 comments Hi Guys, like many of you I work with AI agents every day and across several clients. The major time cost for me is to re-explaining context and past decisions, client rules, that we already do. To finish every tools as its own memory. So I’m curious how you actually handle this: 1. When you start a new session, how do you give context to the agent (context came from chat, mail, ticket ...) ? 2. Do you use more than one agent type (claude, codex ...) ? And if yes, how do you carry context between agents ? 3. If you work for several clients, how do you keep their context separate ? 4. The last time something went wrong ( an agent used a rejected approach, forgot a decision ...), what happened, and how much time did it cost to you ? 5. Did you paid or built a tool that helped you with these problems ? Do you still use it ? I’m exploring whether to build something, so I’m trying to learn how other people really work. Thanks for your return. murillians 0 minutes ago | next [–] Spec driven design helps, OpenSpec/Git SDD Kit/ GitShipDone helps with the previous decision problems and design context. Most of these live in the project repos so they won’t pollute each other reply charlesabarnes 7 minutes ago | prev [–] I use a gitignored ADR (Architecture Decision Record) directory in all of my repos right now. I mainly use Claude code, but I am dabbling in self hosted llms with oh my pi. There's no additional tools needed because usually llms "get it" natively. Also I tend to use a gitignored status doc for resuming where I left off. I tend to leave this stuff gitignored since it's all pretty "sloppy" and not really for consumption with others. reply Guidelines | FAQ | Lists | API | Security | Legal | Apply to YC | Contact
